questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nutrients and Balanced Diet' refers to.
questions.a: Food supplies six classes of nutrients -- carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water -- each with its own work in the body. A balanced diet combines them in right amounts for one's age and activity, using food groups, so that energy, repair and protection are all met without excess.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nutrients and Balanced Diet'.
questions.a: Six nutrients, five food groups, one aim -- a plate balanced for your age and work.

concepts.title: Nutritional Needs of Adolescents and Meal Planning

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nutritional Needs of Adolescents and Meal Planning' refers to.
questions.a: The adolescent growth spurt raises demands for energy, protein, calcium and iron; girls additionally need iron against menstrual losses. Meal planning for this stage favours frequent, nutrient-dense meals, breakfast never skipped, and moderation in sugary, fried and processed snacks.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nutritional Needs of Adolescents and Meal Planning'.
questions.a: Feed the growth spurt -- calcium for bones, iron for blood, breakfast for the brain.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Health, Fitness and Hygiene Practices' refers to.
questions.a: Health is more than absence of disease -- a state of physical, mental and social well-being. Fitness grows from regular exercise, adequate sleep and hygiene habits; food safety in storage and preparation protects the health that nutrition builds.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Health, Fitness and Hygiene Practices'.
questions.a: Nutrition builds, exercise trains, hygiene protects -- the three legs of everyday health.
